text: We installed 902 agent skills/plugins/MCP servers in throwaway sandboxes across 5 coding agents. 803 worked. The other 99 have stories, and we're going to tell all of them.
Codex went 65 for 65 on plugin installs this week. Perfect score. Codex, please stop, the other agents are watching.
Grok Build quietly auto-loads your Claude Code plugins. 295 of the plugins we track rely on exactly that. Install once in Claude Code, get it in Grok for free. Underrated.
Hot take: "works with AI agents" on a README means nothing until someone actually runs the install. So we did. In a sandbox. With no API keys. Like animals.
11 skills passed in every agent we could test them in (4+): Cloudflare, CodeRabbit, Figma, Notion, Qodo, Sentry, Supabase, Superpowers, Vercel + 2 CrowdStrike ones. The overachievers club.

PSA for Grok Build users: auth0, grafana-mcp, postman and pr-review-toolkit started failing. Nothing broke. The names now exist in 2+ marketplaces, so grok asks which one. Fix: grok plugin install auth0@<marketplace>

Install tip: in Claude Code it's
/plugin install sentry@claude-plugins-official
The @marketplace part isn't decoration. Leave it off and you're playing roulette.
MCP servers are harder than plugins. A plugin just has to install. An MCP server has to install AND connect. Cursor's MCP pass rate this week: 29/52. The other 23 said hi and then ghosted.
Superpowers (~305k ★) and mattpocock-skills (~303k ★) are the most-starred things in our directory. Both are in the Claude Code marketplace. Stars aren't tests, though. We test.
We send one email a week: what broke, what's new, which installs to copy-paste. No hype, just logs. Issue #1 is coming.
Works in X, not in Y: chrome-devtools-mcp installs fine in Claude Code and Grok Build, but fails our Pi install test. Same skill, different agent, different day.
Pi installs plugins straight from git repos. Cool, until the repo isn't shaped like Pi expects. 57/87 passed this week. Most failures are layout, not bugs.
Agent tooling in 2026: 5 agents, 3 plugin marketplaces, 1 MCP spec, and 0 people who know which install command to type. Hi, we're the 1 person now.
New this week: videogen landed in the Grok Build marketplace. Text → video, script → MP4. It passed its install test first try. Showing off a little.
If you maintain an agent skill: want to know if it installs in Codex, Cursor, Grok Build and Pi too? Submit it. We'll run it through all five and show you the logs, good or bad.
Pick your agent on SkillMaxx and every install command on the site rewrites itself for it. Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Cursor, Pi. One click, zero translating READMEs.
The official MCP reference servers (fetch, filesystem, git, memory, sequential-thinking, time) are still the backbone of half the setups out there. Boring is a feature.
How we test, in one breath: fresh sandbox, real agent CLI, no credentials. "Pass" = the agent itself lists it as installed/enabled (or connected, for MCP). Every result links its log.
Overall install pass rate this week: 89% (803/902). Down from 90% on Oct 16. Not because skills got worse, mostly because marketplaces got crowded.
cyanheads' PubMed MCP: connects in Cursor ✓, fails to connect in Claude Code ✗ (this week). Same server. If it's misbehaving for you, it might be your agent, not you.

Codex: 100%
Grok Build: 95%
Claude Code: 92%
Pi: 66%
Cursor (MCP): 56%
Not a ranking of the agents. It's a ranking of how well the ecosystem ships for each one.
Unpopular opinion: a skill directory that hides its failures is just a vibes directory. Ours shows the red ✗ next to the green ✓, with logs.
Tool authors: one green ✓ in five agents is free distribution. Most skills are listed for one agent and quietly work in three. We'll tell people.
Database skills are the 4th biggest category we track (39), right behind development, productivity and npm MCP packages. Everyone wants their agent near prod. Bold.
This week in agent skills: the Grok "which auth0?" saga, Codex's perfect week, and a video plugin with main-character energy. In your inbox, once a week.
Install tip for Cursor MCP: drop the server in ~/.cursor/mcp.json under mcpServers and check it shows "ready". If it says anything else, it's not ready. Cursor is very literal.
gdharness (the Godot MCP) passed on Oct 16 and failed to connect this week in Claude Code and Cursor. It also wants a Godot editor running. Fair. It's a Godot harness.
Every night ~2 AM ET we pull the official marketplaces, re-run installs and rebuild the site. Every morning there's a new truth. Most mornings it's "still fine". We love those mornings.
424 skills, plugins and MCP servers across Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Cursor and Pi. Search "github" and you get 3. Search "database" and you get a lot. Go poke it.
Question for the timeline: which skill do you install first in a fresh agent? We'll run the top answers through all 5 agents and post the results.
Week 1 recap: 424 skills tracked, 902 sandboxed installs, 803 passes, 1 new Grok plugin, 4 ambiguous names, 0 API keys harmed.
Gotcha: an MCP server can be "installed" and still useless. Always check your agent's MCP list for connected/ready. That's the line we grade on, not "exit code 0".
Pinned-worthy truth: the best agent skill is the one that installs on the first try in the agent you actually use.
If you only read one email about agent tooling a week, make it the one with receipts. SkillMaxx Weekly: what broke, what's new, what to copy-paste.
Shipping a plugin to the Claude Code marketplace? You're probably already in Grok Build too (it auto-loads Claude Code plugins). Check your listing and see where else you work.
